note: Committed spec for the relational substrate. build_substrate.py reads this and emits Visual_Second_Brain_Substrate.xlsx. Sheets are the source of truth; Docs/Sites/My Maps are projections. Edit this spec, re-run the builder, and the workbook is regenerated deterministically.
readme: Black Fox Studios | Pre-code Google Sheets substrate. Sheets are the source of truth; Docs / Sites / My Maps are projections.
Every entity gets an immutable typed ID (PER-, ORG-, PLA-, PRJ-, RES-, EVT-, VIS-). Names change; IDs never do.
Each row in a type sheet is exactly one thing, keyed back to MASTER_REGISTRY.
Never comma-list relationships inside an entity row. Many-to-many goes in RELATIONS.
4. Every relation cites a source event
source_event_id is REQUIRED on RELATIONS. Every connection traces to an EVENT, which traces to a source document.
Dossier Docs, project Sites, and My Maps are projections generated FROM these sheets, never the reverse.
A human editing a sheet directly is a valid input, equal to an automated update. The engine reconciles either way.

sheets.name: 01_MASTER_REGISTRY
sheets.title: MASTER_REGISTRY
sheets.description: The spine. Every entity gets exactly one row here. ID format: TYPE-##### (e.g., PER-00001).

sheets.name: 02_PEOPLE
sheets.title: PEOPLE
sheets.description: Individuals. entity_id is a foreign key to MASTER_REGISTRY. primary_org_id points to an ORG- id.

sheets.name: 03_ORGANIZATIONS
sheets.title: ORGANIZATIONS
sheets.description: Institutional entities. primary_location_id points to a PLA- id.

sheets.name: 04_PLACES
sheets.title: PLACES
sheets.description: Physical locations. lat/lng feed My Maps pins.

sheets.name: 05_PROJECTS
sheets.title: PROJECTS
sheets.description: Bounded efforts. project_site_url = the Google Site; site_map_sheet_url = the per-project SITE sheets workbook.

sheets.name: 06_RESOURCES
sheets.title: RESOURCES
sheets.description: Grants, tools, documents, proof artifacts, architectural commitments, canonical books, principles, drifts, external validations. PRE-POPULATED with the foundation.

sheets.name: 07_EVENTS
sheets.title: EVENTS
sheets.description: The keystone. A bounded occurrence with participants, date, project context, source document. Relations are derived from events. produced_by_* reference Codex R-/S- IDs.

sheets.name: 08_RELATIONS
sheets.title: RELATIONS
sheets.description: Connective tissue. Each row = one relation between two entities. source_event_id is REQUIRED — every connection traces to an event.

sheets.name: 09_VISUAL_ARTIFACTS
sheets.title: VISUAL_ARTIFACTS
sheets.description: Infographics, dashboards, slide decks, maps, audio/video overviews. First-class entities that persist, version with their data, and regenerate.

sheets.name: 10_LINT_FINDINGS
sheets.title: LINT_FINDINGS
sheets.description: System-flagged issues for human review. Starts empty. Populated by the engine once running.

sheets.name: 11_INTEGRATIONS
sheets.title: INTEGRATIONS
sheets.description: Every external service the system depends on, with failure mode and fallback. Doubles as the technical-architecture inventory for funder proposals.

sheets.name: P_SITE_PAGES
sheets.title: SITE_PAGES  (per-project template)
sheets.description: Page-level structure of one project Google Site. Copy this tab into each project workbook.

sheets.name: P_SITE_CONTENT_BLOCKS
sheets.title: SITE_CONTENT_BLOCKS  (per-project template)
sheets.description: The content blocks on each page. The Site is rebuilt by walking this sheet in order. The Sheet is the intended state; the Site is the projection.

sheets.name: P_SITE_SYNC_LOG
sheets.title: SITE_SYNC_LOG  (per-project template)
sheets.description: Operational health log of each site sync. Records what was attempted, what failed, and what manual edits were detected on the Site.

When regenerating auto tabs, any relation/entry without a confirming event in the last 180 days is visually flagged as possibly stale (never deleted). Edit this number to change the rule.
Foundation produces value at pre-code; AI is named honestly as accelerator. Communities are never sold capabilities they cannot operate or verify.

EDI contract rule: provide coaching, review, feedback; do NOT ghostwrite applications. The synthesis layer may structure, critique, and visualize a client's own work but must not author work that must be the client's own. Governs any funded technical-assistance work.
